points.description: States that array elements can be accessed directly (random access / by index, constant time), unlike linked lists which need traversal from the start.
points.partial_credit: Award about 2-3 marks for a related but vague advantage (e.g. arrays are faster, simpler or use contiguous memory) without saying elements are accessed directly/by index.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying array elements can be reached directly (by index, random access, O(1)) in any wording; mentioning linked-list traversal is not required. Give part marks for vague but related answers such as "arrays are faster" or "contiguous memory" without the direct-access idea. Give none for answers about unrelated points, such as arrays being resizable, or that contradict direct access.
